tier1.text: The zona pellucida is a coat that protects the egg. This clear coat wraps around the egg, under an outer layer of cells. A sperm must get through the zona pellucida before fertilization can happen. After fertilization, the egg releases material into the zona pellucida, creating a barrier that blocks more sperm.

sentences.text: The zona pellucida is a coat that protects the egg.

quotes.quote: In mammals, the egg is protected by a layer of extracellular matrix consisting mainly of glycoproteins called the zona pellucida.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: This clear coat wraps around the egg, under an outer layer of cells.

quotes.quote: outer layer of follicular (granulosa) cells that form around a developing oocyte in the ovary and remain with it upon ovulation. The underlying zona pellucida (pellucid = “transparent”) is a transparent, but thick, glycoprotein membrane that surrounds the cell’s plasma membrane.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: A sperm must get through the zona pellucida before fertilization can happen.

quotes.quote: zona pellucida: thick, gel-like glycoprotein membrane that coats the oocyte and must be penetrated by sperm before fertilization can occur
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: After fertilization, the egg releases material into the zona pellucida, creating a barrier that blocks more sperm.

quotes.quote: cortical reaction: following fertilization, the release of cortical granules from the oocyte’s plasma membrane into the zona pellucida creating a fertilization membrane that prevents any further attachment or penetration of sperm; part of the slow block to polyspermy
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
